questions.enonce_markdown:
Define the following terms as used in Biotechnology.

(i) Plasmid.

(ii) Vector.

(iii) Ligase.

(iv) Bacteriophage

(v) Clone. *(2, 2, 1,2 ,2 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Plasmid**: a small, circular, double-stranded molecule of DNA found in bacteria, separate from the main bacterial chromosome, which can replicate independently and can be used to carry a foreign gene into another cell.

(ii) **Vector**: a carrier (such as a plasmid or a virus) used to transfer a piece of foreign DNA (a gene) into a host cell in genetic engineering.

(iii) **Ligase**: an enzyme that joins two DNA fragments together by sealing the sugar-phosphate backbone (for example, it joins a gene to a plasmid cut with a restriction enzyme).

(iv) **Bacteriophage**: a virus that infects bacteria and inserts its DNA into them; it can be used as a vector to carry genes into bacteria.

(v) **Clone**: a group of cells, organisms or DNA molecules that are genetically identical, all derived from one parent by asexual reproduction (or by copying one original piece of DNA).

questions.enonce_markdown: Differentiate between a food chain and a food web. *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Food chain | Food web |
|---|---|
| A **single, linear sequence** of organisms showing who eats whom | A **network of interconnected food chains** in a community |
| Each organism feeds on **one** kind of food and is eaten by **one** kind of consumer | An organism may feed on **several** foods and be eaten by **several** consumers |
| Shows only **one path** of energy flow | Shows **many alternative paths** of energy flow |
| Simple, easy to draw: e.g. grass $\rightarrow$ grasshopper $\rightarrow$ toad $\rightarrow$ hawk | Complex, realistic picture of feeding relationships in an ecosystem |
| If one organism is lost the chain is broken | If one organism is lost, consumers can switch to other foods, so the web is **more stable** |

In both, the arrows point in the direction of energy transfer, from the organism eaten to the organism that eats it, and both start with a producer (green plant).

questions.enonce_markdown: In an abandoned school farm, the following organisms were discovered to be living there after a period of three years; hawks, green vegetation such as huckle berry and cabbage. nymphs of grasshopper, flying grasshoppers, toads under green vegetation, earthworms under rotten logs of wood and lizards. Using the above organisms, construct a suitable food web to establish the relationship between these organisms. *(5 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Feeding relationships (arrows point from the organism eaten to the organism that eats it):**

- green vegetation (huckleberry, cabbage) $\rightarrow$ nymphs of grasshopper
- green vegetation (huckleberry, cabbage) $\rightarrow$ flying grasshoppers
- rotten logs of wood (dead organic matter) $\rightarrow$ earthworms
- nymphs of grasshopper $\rightarrow$ toads
- nymphs of grasshopper $\rightarrow$ lizards
- flying grasshoppers $\rightarrow$ toads
- flying grasshoppers $\rightarrow$ lizards
- flying grasshoppers $\rightarrow$ hawks
- earthworms $\rightarrow$ toads
- earthworms $\rightarrow$ lizards
- toads $\rightarrow$ hawks
- lizards $\rightarrow$ hawks

**Diagram to draw** (with arrows):

```
                         HAWKS
                       ^   ^   ^
                       |   |   |
          TOADS --------+   |   +-------- LIZARDS
          ^   ^   ^         |         ^   ^   ^
          |   |   |         |         |   |   |
 nymphs of    flying grasshoppers   earthworms
 grasshopper        ^                  ^
      ^             |                  |
      +--- green vegetation       rotten logs (decaying matter)
           (huckleberry, cabbage)
```

(Both nymphs and flying grasshoppers feed on the green vegetation and are eaten by toads and lizards; flying grasshoppers, toads and lizards are all eaten by hawks; earthworms feed on the decaying wood and are eaten by toads and lizards.)

**Roles:** producers = green vegetation (huckleberry, cabbage); primary consumers (herbivores) = nymphs and flying grasshoppers; earthworms feed on dead organic matter (detritivores); secondary consumers = toads, lizards; tertiary (top) consumer = hawks.

**Marking points:** producers placed at the base; correct arrows (direction of energy flow); each consumer linked to more than one food source; the hawk at the top; the earthworm linked to the rotten wood.
